title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
description: BadBox 3.0 is a large-scale ad fraud botnet operation targeting low-cost, uncertified Android devices. It uses backdoors to install modules that generate fraudulent video ad bid requests and enroll devices into residential proxy networks. At its peak, BadBox 3.0 generated approximately 40 billion daily bid requests, representing over 4% of all connected TV traffic observed by the monitoring platform. The botnet mimics legitimate video ad SDKs to make fraudulent traffic appear as premium inventory from well-known apps, often using residential IP addresses to evade detection. The operation was disrupted through takedown efforts targeting its command-and-control infrastructure. The threat actor behind BadBox 3.0 is linked to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ and operates multiple proxy networks.
